measured_direct_calls.note: fully-cached repeat of prefix8: zero Node-bridge round trips, zero cache misses, wall time still ~0.84s -- ~same as the original prefix8 call. This is the row that rules out the Node bridge / AST cache as the cost driver.

root_cause_chain.claim: OpenUIIncrementalEngine._lex_tokens (engine.py:99-110) calls self._parser.lex(prefix) -- Lark's standalone .lex() convenience API -- with the FULL current prefix string, on every _full_sync (engine.py:124) and every _incremental_sync (engine.py:149) call, i.e. on every _sync (engine.py:177) call.
root_cause_chain.evidence: cProfile: engine.py:99 _lex_tokens called 23546 times for one build_completion_forest invocation, 27.1s cumulative; every call routes into lark/lexer.py's lex/next_token/scanner/_build_scanner chain.

root_cause_chain.claim: The Lark grammar object itself IS cached (_load_parser, engine.py:43-53, @lru_cache(maxsize=4)), but nothing caches or reuses a built Lexer/Scanner across .lex() calls -- each call reconstructs the terminal-disambiguation scanner from scratch via _build_lexer -> _build_scanner -> _create_unless, which recompiles regex patterns every time.
root_cause_chain.evidence: lark/lexer.py:592 _build_scanner called 23546 times (1:1 with _lex_tokens calls); lark/lexer.py:334 _create_unless called 23546 times, 14.685s cumulative, driving 6.4M calls to re._compile and 5.5M calls to re.match.

root_cause_chain.claim: The recursive lookahead-then-verify witness search in pack.py's _tail_from/_tail (bounded nodes_left=16 per I3) calls _build_openui_completion_forest up to 171 times for a SINGLE top-level build_completion_forest call at this prefix, multiplying the per-call lexer-rebuild cost into seconds of wall time.
root_cause_chain.evidence: cProfile: pack.py:402 _tail called 4419 times (recursive), compiler_draft.py:1480 _build_openui_completion_forest called 171 times, for one top-level build_completion_forest(prefix9) call.

root_cause_chain.claim: The Node bridge (lang_core.parse, the out-of-process Node subprocess used by _generated_ast_is_complete) and its lru_cache are NOT the bottleneck: a fully-cached repeat call with zero bridge round trips and zero cache misses (prefix8_repeat) still costs ~0.84s, essentially the same as the original call that made 23 real bridge round trips totaling only 0.037s.
root_cause_chain.evidence: measured_direct_calls[3] (prefix8_repeat) vs measured_direct_calls[1] (prefix8): wall_s 0.8406 vs 0.9561, bridge_calls_wall_s_sum 0.0 vs 0.0374.

interpretation: PR #1171 correctly identified compiler_ms (not denoiser_ms/forwards_count) as the wall-clock sink and that it scales with compiler_prefill_batches; that stands. This diagnostic resolves the specific open question about compiler_ms's internal breakdown: it is neither Node-bridge round-trip cost nor _generated_ast_is_complete cache misses (both are cheap and well-amortized), but the OpenUIIncrementalEngine's uncached, full-prefix Lark lexer/scanner rebuild inside _lex_tokens, multiplied by the recursive _tail_from/_tail candidate-witness search's call count. The growth from prefix8 to prefix9 is worse than linear in the underlying call count (6.8x more _generated_ast_is_complete calls, 13.7x more wall time), consistent with the recursive _tail fan-out multiplying a fixed uncached per-node lexer-rebuild cost rather than a flat per-candidate cost.
scope_note: Single-process micro-benchmark, n=1 rep per prefix, 4 prefixes -- not a multi-rep confirm and does not prove this is the ONLY compiler_ms contributor on every record. But the near-zero marginal cost of prefix8_repeat is sufficient on its own to rule out the Node bridge and AST cache as primary drivers, and the cProfile breakdown directly attributes the remaining cost.
why_finding_not_patch: Same precedent as decode-compiler-tree-deadline-swallow-finding.md and decode-timeout-hang-seed44-steps72-finding.md: engine.py backs dsl.grammar_capabilities (watched in src/slm_training/resources/versions.json via pack.py / compiler_draft.py) and is exercised by every default constrained-decode path's speculative/lookahead witness search (I3). A real fix needs a benchmark-backed unit test and should land via improve-openui-harnesses, not be patched blind here.
proposed_fix_sketch: Cache a built Lexer/Scanner per grammar path alongside _load_parser's cached Lark object (engine.py:43-53); have _lex_tokens (engine.py:99) reuse it instead of calling self._parser.lex(prefix), which rebuilds the scanner every call.

Make _incremental_sync (engine.py:149) genuinely incremental at the lex layer too -- it already tracks _fed_token_count and only feeds new tokens to the InteractiveParser, but it still re-lexes the entire prefix from scratch (_lex_tokens(prefix) on the full string, engine.py:152) before slicing to the new tokens.

Re-run this diagnostic's prefix9 case after the fix and confirm _lex_tokens/_build_scanner call counts and compiler_ms both drop without changing n_paths/coverage (caching change only, never a legality change per I6/I3).
Re-run the PR #1171 isolated per-record eval protocol to see whether compiler_ms drops enough for the exposure12 hero to finish inside decode_timeout_seconds=30.
next_steps: Re-run PR #1171's per-record isolated eval diagnostic after the fix to see whether decode_outcome shifts away from fallback_output / empty_completion_forest.

If compiler_ms drops substantially, re-check whether PR #1171's separate deadline-swallow bug (TimeoutError caught by the bare except in compiler_draft.py:2313) is still reachable in practice, or whether it was mostly masking this lexer-rebuild cost.
